newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late palm olein down, tone weak.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late palm olein down, tone weak.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices edged downwards in late trading on Thursday as buyers turned cautious and waited for values to decline further, traders said.
They said olein was around 1,435-40 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, compared with 1,445-50 at the opening. Some quotes were heard at 1,425-30 rupiah for small quantities.
"My shipment of 4,000 tonnes of olein will be unloaded tomorrow," one trader said. "Supply is expected to build up by next week and prices are likely to be depressed."
Another trader attributed the weaker prices to a call by President Suharto for market operations to control prices.
Suharto ordered the state logistics agency BULOG to carry out market operations in essential commodities, including cooking oil, to ensure prices stay stable.
"I think his statement affected sentiment as BULOG might be importing more oil following his call," the trader said. "Buyers are now expecting prices to ease further.

Traders said a move by the state-run joint marketing agency (KPB) to suspend crude palm oil exports in October to enable it to clear a backlog of previous commitments had no impact today. It pushed up Malaysian and European prices on Wednesday.
